title: Preserve musical intent and symbolic score separately from MIDI
summary: Proposed SunOmega design motivated by the richer notation-vs-MIDI distinction. A semantic score can retain phrase-level intent while exact event fields compile to MIDI; user/audio value requires testing.

build.target: Translate a human melody brief into explicit, inspectable score events that a deterministic helper can compile to MIDI.
requires: GF-style semantic MIDI build and Mido for export
inputs: A complete original score with meter, tonic, mode, exact onset/duration and pitches
outputs: MIDI file with exact-event receipt when compiled
execute: Let the composing model propose concrete note events; retain the higher-level phrase intention as unexecuted metadata.
Validate the note schedule, pitch range, constraints, rests and ownership through the semantic-midi helper.
Reject ambiguity or impossible constraints; do not invent missing pitches.
Export MIDI and compare notes/timing by independent round-trip reader.
Test separately whether Suno conditioning preserves the motif under authorized generation.

applies_when: Agent must control a melody more precisely than a text-only style prompt.
An original, bounded monophonic motif or hook is needed.
avoid_when: Complex polyphony, chromaticism or modulation exceeds v0 helper limits.
The agent only has prose and no permission to resolve missing notes.

enforced: Monophonic 1–16 bars and 1–128 notes, bounded rational timing and exact 480 PPQN
No overwrite of different existing MIDI bytes
operator: No Suno upload, credit use or external account action in this build.

stop_when: Valid original MIDI exists with verified event receipt, or the score is rejected.
No hidden musical inference or auto-quantization.

checks: Use deterministic Mido note-on/off round trip and SHA-256 reproducibility.
Separately collect provider and listener evidence before claiming fidelity.
